cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Sonder – the profound feeling of realizing that everyone has a complex life.

p.em: Example: Walking through the crowded station, he was struck by a sudden sense of sonder.

cosy-blockquote.p: Passerby – a person who happens to be going past something or someone.

p.em: Example: The street musician played his violin as every passerby ignored him.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vivid – producing powerful feelings or strong, clear images in the mind.

p.em: Example: He had a vivid memory of his first day at school.
Example: The novel's plot was so intricate that I had to read it twice.

cosy-blockquote.p: Anonymity – the condition of being anonymous or unknown.

p.em: Example: The artist preferred anonymity and never showed his face in public.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ephemeral – lasting for a very short time.

p.em: Example: Our interaction was ephemeral, but it left a lasting impression on me.

cosy-blockquote.p: Internalize – make (attitudes or behavior) part of one's nature by learning or unconscious assimilation.

p.em: Example: It takes time to internalize the values of a new culture.

cosy-blockquote.p: Multifaceted – having many sides or aspects.

p.em: Example: The problem is multifaceted and cannot be solved with a simple answer.

cosy-blockquote.p: Subconscious – concerning the part of the mind of which one is not fully aware.

p.em: Example: Our subconscious fears often influence our daily decisions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Perspective – a particular way of regarding something; a point of view.

p.em: Example: Traveling to different countries gives you a much broader perspective on life.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How often do you experience a sense of sonder while commuting or walking in a crowded city?
★ When was the last time you had to confront sonder in your own personal journey?

Do you ever wonder about the destination and purpose of a random passerby you see on the street?
★ How comfortable are you with allowing passerby to guide your daily decisions?

Can you describe a vivid moment when you realized you were just a background character in someone else's story?
★ Have you ever felt a deep sense of conflict regarding vivid in a relationship?

Why is it so easy to forget the intricate details of other people's lives when we are stressed?
★ Can you share a moment from your childhood where intricate felt completely natural?

Does the anonymity of a large city make it easier or harder to feel empathy for others?
★ How do you personally nurture anonymity when you feel emotionally exhausted?

How do ephemeral interactions with strangers sometimes leave the deepest impact on our mood?
★ Have you ever had to choose between social conformity and personal ephemeral?

Is it possible to truly internalize the idea that every single person is as important as you are?
★ Who in your life best embodies the essence of internalize, and what have they taught you?

In what ways are the personalities of your closest friends more multifaceted than they first appeared?
★ In what area of your life do you feel multifaceted is most desperately needed right now?

How does our subconscious bias affect how we judge people we only see for a few seconds?
★ How has your personal understanding of subconscious shifted over the last five years?

How can changing your perspective to include the lives of others reduce your own personal anxieties?
★ If you had to describe your personal experience with perspective in one word, what would it be?

★ Would you be willing to use technology to artificially boost your capacity for passerby?

Future educational systems will prioritize the cultivation of vivid over traditional academic skills. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with vivid?

ul.li: Incorrect: Every people has a life → Correct: Every person has a life / All people have lives ((Subject-verb agreement))
Incorrect: It makes me to think about others → Correct: It makes me think about others ((Make + object + bare infinitive))
Incorrect: I am interesting in their stories → Correct: I am interested in their stories ((-ed vs -ing))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
Incorrect: It is depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Verb vs Adjective))
